one_line: HDI takes the MUST set from 26 of 50 to 32 (today's U1 ban) or 35 (34 gate-clean, ban lifted), unties one of four hubs (FT-REF), walls off 6-7 deferrable connections where the through plan walls off 1 and seals the U2-5 GND tie; the board still cannot be configured, JTAG-programmed or hold its USB bridge out of reset, so the $309.34 JLC HDI 2-step order is not worth placing on this evidence -- HDI does not close the MUST set and nothing measured here does.

The survivors are three local knots, identical on every via model (pad centres from route_inputs.json): U1's SW corner balls W10/W11/V10/V12 in a 1.0 x 0.5 mm patch at (46.4-47.4, 7.4-7.9) carrying CFG-M0/CFG-M1/FPGA-TDI/RST# to R20/R21 (Bottom, y 4), R4 and X2-23; U1's NE corner balls D18/D19/E18/G18/G19 at (50.4-50.9, 13.4-14.9) carrying the flash bus, PUDC_B and UART_FT_RXD to U4 directly north (x 43.85/51.15, y 17.5-21.3); U2's south row pins 14/18/21/22 carrying FT-RESETN/TDO/PROG#/DONE 31-36 mm east through the south band (x 31..58, y 2.0..4.6 stitch 63-69 %) that TMS and TCK already took. None of the field arm's 10 in-field via objects served a knot net.
is_the_order_worth_placing: No, not on this evidence. JLC HDI 2-step is $309.34 qty 5 / $313.19 qty 10, 12-13 days, against $186.13 / $201.97 and 8-9 days for the standard JLC06161H-3313E board (+$123.21, +66.2 %, +4 days; HDI structure fee $167.30) plus buried-via and lamination fees JLC only quote manually (docs/hdi_fab_facts.md 37-40, docs/hdi_spec.md 259-262). The order's premise -- microvias get the board routed -- is not supported: HDI closes 6-9 more of the 50 MUST connections, unties one hub, and leaves 15-18 open including every configuration strap, three of four flash data lines, FPGA-TDI, PROG#, DONE, FT-RESETN and UART RXD; on the same plans it walls off 5-6 more deferrable connections than the through plan and seals a MUST GND tie. A board that cannot be configured is not worth fabricating in any technology, so the order is moot until the three knots are untied; if they untie on the through model, the $186.13 board is the one to order. Keep the six via types and HDI rules in the Layer Stack Manager -- they cost nothing until an order names them. Neither HDI plan is placeable (B-field fails route_emit; both fail the permanence rule and seal U2-5); they are evidence only.
field_decision_value: +3 connections in plan copper (FLASH-CS# U4-1<->U1-K19, UART_FT_TXD U2-38<->track, FPGA-DONE R4-15<->R4-7), 0 lost: 32 -> 35 of 50; +2 gate-clean (32 -> 34) because the field plan's TDO R91-1<->R4-4 carries an illegal 0.1414 mm same-path via pair (instrument gap; B-banned closes it legally with 1 via). It spent 10 in-field via objects (8 buried L3/L4 + 2 Top/L2/L3 laser) on UART_FT_TXD, FPGA-TDO, TMS, FPGA-CCLK, CLK-12M-FT -- none on a knot net -- and costs one more walled-off deferrable (6 -> 7) and one more L2 OFF-PLANE GND pad centre (C91-2 under UART_FT_TXD's stack). Consistent with stage 9's +2 for the same lift on the through model (26 -> 28). Worth +2..+3 of 50, not a lever; user decision 7 can stay open without changing any conclusion.
what_next: Do not place the JLC HDI 2-step order and do not place either HDI plan; keep the HDI via types and rules in the Layer Stack Manager as a modelled, unpriced option.

risks: Single commit order (index) and fixed budget (90, 36): stage 9 saw an 11-connection spread across orders on the full set, so every arm's absolute count could move; the between-arm deltas are paired at identical order and budget. 'No route on the lattice' proves existence failures, never impossibility.

Merged-span model only (one 3-layer span per laser stack), because the gates accept only that form as a Top<->L3 join; the two-object form (Altium's uVia 1:2 + 2:3) was built byte-identical to repro's but not run. Blocking, pitch, antipad and layer set are identical by construction from the model files; the emitted record and route_emit's object count are not.

Neither HDI plan is placeable: B-field fails route_emit (same-path via pair 0.1414 mm apart), both fail the permanence rule (route_reach -6 / -7) and seal the U2-5 GND tie, and 1-2 GND pad centres sit in L2 laser anti-pad voids (both planes remain one island, 100.0 %). Evidence only.

Fab facts outside the model: JLC's 6L 2-step layer pairing is an open fab question, buried-via and lamination fees are manual-quote only, and the 87-legal-site count under U1 was not exercised (the router placed 10 in-field objects on five nets, none on a knot net).
Timings are contended (both arms and a verifier ran concurrently on the same 24-core box); the through-plan route_reach was a warm run (board pass from cache), so no cold-pass time is claimed for it.
The two router-invisible MUST GND ties (R15-1, U2-5) are outside every count here; U2-5 becomes untie-able by hand under both HDI plans, which the whole-board ledger charges at -1.
The three-knot diagnosis is from pad coordinates and blocker strings, not from a per-pair experiment; where each exclusion bites at the cell level is still not located (stage 9's own caveat).
